rejections.reason: Definition of truncated difference claims uniqueness via lem-nat-add-cancellative, which only gives right cancellation (if m+k=n+k then m=n), not that m+j=m+j' implies j=j'. Left cancellation or commutativity not provided.
In step 1.1, the definition of the splice map h on p+q uses a case distinction: h(k)=f(k) if k
Title claims Pascal's rule checked at every entry, but proof step 2.1 only applies Pascal's rule to interior entries; boundary entries are given by [L1] and not checked with Pascal's rule.
Fact [L5] cites def-natural-numbers and lem-nat-add-commutative for 'σ(j)=j+1=1+j', but neither item defines addition or states that equality; step 1.2 uses it unjustified, missing def-nat-addition.

Fact [L2] states only left cancellation (ab=ac implies b=c) but step 2.1 uses right cancellation; the fact does not faithfully restate lem-group-cancellation which includes both. The step is unlicensed as written.
The statement claims the four groups are infinite and abelian, but the proof only verifies they are abelian groups, with no justification or citation for infiniteness.
Remark states thm-division-algorithm-in-z is proved on this page, but it is not among the page siblings; a false claim about library contents.

Step 3.1 claims the elements of the natural number n are exactly the naturals s < n (additive order), which is not among the cited facts; it requires lem-nat-order-is-membership, not cited. Thus surjectivity of the map is not fully justified.

Fact [L2] states only totality, antisymmetry, and transitivity of the order, but steps 1.2 and 5.1 use compatibility with addition and positivity of product, which are not included in [L2] or cited elsewhere. Hence those steps are unlicensed.
Fact [L4] states that 0 < x implies 1 <= x, but the cited lem-nat-embeds-int does not include this statement; the fact is stronger than its source, a citation fidelity defect.

Fact L8 claims 2 ≠ 1 and 3 ≠ 1 in N, but the cited lemma (lem-nat-embeds-int) only states that iota is injective and preserves order; it does not assert those specific inequalities, making L8 stronger than its source and the proof step citing it unjustified.

Step 1.1 claims d>=1 from a,b nonzero, citing only [L1],[L3]. Neither states that gcd of nonzero integers is >=1 or that d divides a,b. Necessary facts from def-common-divisor-and-gcd are not cited, making the step unjustified.

The remark claims that lem-of-zero-mult records that right distributivity follows from commutativity, but that lemma only proves that zero times a equals zero, not anything about distributivity. This is a false claim about the library's contents.

Title incorrectly claims that restriction of scalars along the embedded copy of Q gives a vector space over Q. Restriction of scalars yields a structure over the embedded copy Q_R, not over Q. The proof correctly defines the Q-structure directly, so the title asserts a false method.

The item claims 'Both failures are recorded on this page as [[fs-closed-ball-is-the-closure-of-the-open-ball]]', but that sibling only records the closure failure, not the sphere failure. This is a false claim about the page's contents.
L1 claims 'j -> j+1 runs over naturals >=1' citing def-natural-numbers, which lacks that property. Step 2.2 relies on it for surjectivity, so countability is unjustified.
Step 2.1 claims d(p,q)≥0 without citing lem-metric-nonnegativity; the cited facts L3 and L4 do not license it.

Fact L1 asserts a bijection has a two-sided inverse function that is itself a bijection, but the cited def-injection-surjection-bijection only asserts the inverse's existence and its two defining equations; that the inverse is itself a bijection is not stated there, so L1 is stronger than its cited source.

The parenthetical proof that e is invertible (e*e=e exhibits e as a two-sided inverse of itself) is not licensed by any cited fact; def-identity-element only gives e as identity, and the invertibility of e is actually proved separately in lem-monoid-units-form-a-group step 1.1, which this definition duplicates without citing.
Step 2.4 claims (g^x)^{-y}=g^{xy} directly from L3/L5 clause but step 6.1 of lem-group-power-laws needed for the negative-exponent case is not among the deps of this item

Fact L4 says every nonempty subset of N has a least element, but step 5.1 applies well-ordering to T which is defined via natural numbers k with iota(k)=a-qb; this is fine, but step 4.1/5.1 never establish T subset of N is used correctly. Actual defect: step 1.3 claims to prove iota reflects order using trichotomy plus L2 antisymmetry, but cites L5 for trichotomy on N not on Z, which is correct; no defect found there. On reflection the proof is sound.

Step 3.2 claims pi' is injective as a composite of injections but pi' is pi composed with delta restricted to n, and neither pi nor delta is shown injective on all of N; also L6 only licenses composites of two injections, not delta which is not addressed as injective there, so the citation is stretched, though delta injectivity is actually shown in 1.10 so this is weak. The real defect: step 4.3 claims w_i=g_{pi'(i)} using step 3.2, but pi' is defined as pi∘delta restricted to n mapping into n, and w_i=h_{delta(i)}=g_{pi(delta(i))}, which equals g_{pi'(i)} only because pi'(i) is defined as pi(delta(i)); this is fine. However the real gap: 1.9 defines k:=pi^{-1}(n) using pi^{-1} without citing that pi is a bijection hence invertible, but L6 does establish bijections are injective/surjective not that they have an inverse function pi^{-1}; def-injection-surjection-bijection remarks establish inverses exist for bijections, so this is licensed.

Fact L4 in lem-cyclic-subgroup-is-the-set-of-powers restates lem-subgroup-criterion as requiring S nonempty with xy^-1 in S, but the cited item's actual test also needs closure verified via that single condition only for subgroup conclusion; however the real issue is in this definition: it asserts by convention <empty set> = {e} is 'a consequence... not a stipulation' citing only def-subgroup, but never invokes lem-intersection-of-subgroups to justify that the intersection of ALL subgroups (i.e. every subgroup of G, since S=empty set is contained in all) equals {e}; it merely notes every subgroup contains e, which shows {e} is a lower bound but not that the intersection equals {e} exactly (needs that {e} itself is a subgroup, which is asserted without citation).

The Definition never proves the recursion theorem's monoid-power clause g^0=e, g^sigma(n)=g^n g is well-formed for all n including using x mapsto x*g as a function M to M requiring closure, which holds trivially, but more importantly the integer-exponent case split cites thm-int-ordered-ring and def-int-order for totality and antisymmetry to guarantee exactly one of 0<=x, x<0 holds, which is correctly licensed; no defect found in citations or logic on inspection.

Step 2.4 cites step 1.4 for x not equal to 0 in Z but never establishes it: it only cites 1.3 and 1.4 which give x,y not equal to 0 in Z, not distinctness of x and -y as elements, and more importantly step 2.4 needs 0<x(-y) which requires x>0,y<0 giving -y>0 by L2 compatibility, a move not licensed by any cited fact in that step.

Step 2.1 cites L2, cancellation in G' stated only as ab=ac implies b=c (left-cancellation), to derive f(e)=e' from e'f(e)=f(e)f(e); that equation has common right factor f(e), so it needs the right-cancellation clause xg=yg implies x=y from lem-group-cancellation, which L2 as restated omits.

Clause (c) claims to derive the constant-sum formula from the constant clause of lem-nat-finite-sum-laws-and-the-canonical-embedding and lem-finite-sum-laws, but the actual derivation needs the reindexing/bridge clause (a) applied to a constant list plus those laws; more importantly the cited N-clause 2 states sum=n*c only for the initial-segment sum, and clause (a) only established S=n with identity map, so citing it for general S without invoking the independence-of-enumeration result first is a licensed but underjustified chain within 30 seconds, not fatal. Accepting since no false claim found; keep true actually.

The truncated-difference paragraph proves uniqueness of n-m (m+j=n and m+j'=n imply j=j') citing only lem-nat-add-cancellative, which is right-cancellation (m+k=n+k implies m=n); concluding j=j' from m+j=m+j' needs commutativity too, as def-nat-order's own remarks confirm by citing both lem-nat-add-commutative and lem-nat-add-cancellative for this identical claim, yet lem-nat-add-commutative is absent from this item's citation and its deps list.
[L1] is a meta-description ('order and arithmetic of Q') rather than the proposition of thm-rat-ordered-field, violating the citation fidelity requirement for fact statements.

Fact [L2] claims 'Order arithmetic: 0 < 1/n ≤ 1/N for n ≥ N ≥ 1' from thm-rat-ordered-field, but that theorem only states Q is a totally ordered field; it does not assert these specific inequalities. The fact restates a consequence not present in the cited source, so the step's citation is unsupported.

Step 2.1 concludes a contradiction from sigma(n) <= k and k < sigma(n), but that requires antisymmetry of <= (sigma(n)<=k and k<=sigma(n) imply k=sigma(n), contradicting k =/= sigma(n)). Antisymmetry is never established or cited: it is not in Facts and Assumptions, and thm-nat-linear-order/lem-nat-trichotomy are not even in the deps list.
Reported a citation-fidelity defect in cor-nat-multiplication-well-defined step 1.1 per the audit instructions; not a request to save/forget memory.
Fact A2 claims 'exactly one of x<y, x=y, y<x' but the cited thm-rat-ordered-field only states the order is total, not the full trichotomy. Thus A2 is a stronger claim not supported by the cited item.

Step 2.1 concludes strict inequalities like m<sigma(n) from a nonzero-witness equation such as sigma(n)=m+sigma(0) without ever establishing m is not equal to sigma(n); that needs cancellation L6, which is available but not cited in step 2.1's tag, in any of its three cases, or in the unused step 1.3.
[L2] violates citation fidelity: it uses canned heading 'Ordered-field arithmetic in Q:' and lists consequences instead of stating the cited theorem thm-rat-ordered-field itself.

Fact [L2] claims that epsilon/2 and delta/4 are positive rationals citing only thm-rat-field, but that theorem only states that Q is a field; it does not give positivity. The fact is stronger than its cited source.

Fact [L4] claims epsilon/(A+B)>0 from thm-rat-ordered-field, but that theorem only states Q is a totally ordered field with three basic properties; it does not directly assert the quotient positivity. The proof step citing [L4] thus relies on a fact not supplied by its citation.

Fact [L7] misstates thm-rat-field by including order properties; proof repeatedly uses ordered field properties of Q (e.g., a'>a, b>0 => a'b>ab) not justified by any cited fact. Missing dependency on thm-rat-ordered-field.

Fact [L1] claims Q has midpoint property and inequalities q-1 less than q less than q+1 but thm-rat-ordered-field only states totality, translation invariance, closure of positives; [L1] is thus stronger than its cited source, and step 1.3 relies on this unsupported claim.

Fact [L5] falsely claims the product formula holds for A,B>=0*; the cited def-cut-multiplication defines it only for A,B>0*, with a separate sign rule for 0*. For A=0* the formula yields a set with a greatest element, not the cut 0*, so [L5] is mathematically incorrect.

Title says R becomes a vector space over Q by restriction of scalars along the embedded copy of Q, but the item's own remarks and proof state claim 3 is proved directly, not by restriction of scalars, since Q itself is not a subfield of R (only Q_R is).

L4 restates lem-divisor-bound as 'd|a, a!=0 implies d<=|a|' but the source proves |d|<=|a|. Step 2.2 uses this weakened/altered form to bound D(a,0) by |a|, silently skipping the needed d<=|d| link, which is never stated or cited anywhere in this item.
Reported a confirmed citation-fidelity defect: L2 omits order-addition compatibility and positive-multiplication closure that steps 1.2 and 5.1 rely on under that tag.

Step 3.2 proves M>0 via product of two positives is positive, citing L2, but L2 as restated in this item only asserts the order is total, antisymmetric and transitive; it omits positives-closed-under-multiplication, which thm-int-ordered-ring actually states but L2 drops.
Fact [L4] is not a restatement of def-null-sequence; it asserts the constant sequence 1 is not null, which does not appear in that definition. Step 2.1 depends on this unsupported claim.
Reported a confirmed circularity: the definition claims the scaling identity independently forces gcd(0,0)=0, but the cited lem-gcd-scaling proof assumes that value at its own (0,0) boundary steps.
Item cites its own audit criteria/output format rather than asking a real question; nothing to action beyond the tool call already made.

Steps 1.2 and 1.3 use the definitions of addition and multiplication on Q from def-rat-operations, but no L# fact restates that definition and the steps cite only L1 (Z ring arithmetic), which does not license the move.
Step 1.1 only fixes some N in ℕ (which includes 0) with |a_m-a_n|<1 for m,n>=N; nothing forces N>=1. If N=0, step 2.2 defines M using a_N=a_0, but the sequence is (a_n) for n>=1, so a_0 is undefined.

L1 attributes the ring identity (-u)v=-(uv) to thm-rat-ordered-field, but that theorem only proves order properties (totality, compatibility with addition, positive products positive) and says nothing about ring arithmetic; step 1.2 also silently needs (-u)(-v)=uv, not licensed by L1 at all.

Steps 1.1-1.5 all rest on the def-integers equivalence a+d=b+c and the def-int-operations/def-int-order formulas for pairs, but Facts&Assumptions only lists A1 (N arithmetic identities) and A2 (N order); the Z-level definitions being applied are never stated as a fact or cited via L#, so the tags on each step do not actually license the pair-manipulation moves being made.

Concluding step asserts Z is a totally ordered commutative ring but only cites order-related steps; thm-int-comm-ring is never cited as an L-fact despite being needed for the ring half of the conclusion.

L2 attributes the specific inequality 0 < 1/n <= 1/N for n >= N >= 1 to thm-rat-ordered-field, but that theorem's text only gives totality, order-addition compatibility, and positivity closure under multiplication; it says nothing about reciprocals or their order-reversing behavior, so L2 states more than its cited source establishes and step 2.1 rests on an uncited derivation.

Step 1.3 claims bounds A,B>=1 citing only lem-cauchy-bounded, which guarantees just A,B>=0; later step 2.2 divides by A+B, an unjustified division by zero if the bound is taken as its minimal value 0.

L1 attributes to thm-rat-ordered-field the facts q-1<q<q+1 and that the midpoint (p+q)/2 lies strictly between p and q, but that theorem's stated content is only totality, translation-invariance (x<=y implies x+z<=y+z), and positivity of products of positives -- it never states or derives the successor/midpoint arithmetic facts steps 1.1 and 1.3 rely on.

The remark cites lem-rat-cut-embeds for the reciprocal identity (q*)^{-1}=(1/q)* for q>0, but that lemma's supplied statement and proof only give the ring-embedding facts (sum, product, order, density) and never state or prove anything about reciprocals or inverses, so the citation supports a claim it does not make.

Step 1.6 asserts |-X|=|X| and that negating a cut flips its sign relative to 0*, used to derive (-X)*Y=-(X*Y), citing only L2/L3/L6 (sign-rule/absval/totality). None of these establishes that negation reverses sign; that fact needs the inverse law L5 plus a nontrivial argument not given or cited, and it isn't a 30-second closure since translation invariance is only proved later (in thm-reals-dedekind-ordered-field) using this theorem as a prerequisite.
Item review identified a genuine citation gap in step 2.1 of the lemma (unlicensed use of metric nonnegativity).

Fact L4 claims 0<x in Z implies 1<=x and cites only lem-nat-embeds-int, but that lemma's text gives only injectivity, order-preservation and nonnegative image, not discreteness; used in step 2.3 to force q=2. Discreteness needs lem-nat-discrete too, per sibling proofs.

Item cites lem-nat-order-is-membership for 3={0,1,2} indexing but that lemma only establishes n={m:m<n}; the actual fact used (def-natural-numbers giving sigma(n)=n union {n}) is fine, so this is minor. Real defect: step 1.4 claims e_1 spans U∩W via L1,L7 but never cites L5 (span-of-single-vector) to license calling it operatorname{span}{e_1}; step 2.2 does cite L5, so that's acceptable. No fatal defect found; accepting.
